concerns.text: When detection-efficiency inputs are unavailable, T005 restricts the OBSERVATIONAL sample to detection space but leaves the synthetic sim catalog intrinsic. Comparing a detection-space obs distribution against an intrinsic sim distribution reintroduces exactly the selection-vs-population confound the plan says it avoids ('Unweighted KS reflects selection bias, not population difference'). The fallback must either apply an equivalent detection-space cut to the sim catalog or explicitly state the comparison is detection-space-obs vs intrinsic-sim and that divergence cannot be attributed to astrophysics.

The plan never states how the reported p-value is derived from the B bootstrap iterations of the weighted KS statistic (e.g., percentile of the observed statistic within the bootstrap null distribution, vs. an asymptotic weighted-KS formula). Without this, the p-value semantics — and whether the bootstrap is a null-distribution bootstrap or merely an uncertainty propagation — are ambiguous and unverifiable. Specify the p-value construction.

MDES is defined for effect-size metrics (e.g., Cohen's d), but the analysis effect is a KS D statistic. The plan does not state which effect-size metric MDES is computed in, nor the target power (e.g., 80%) and test used. Name the metric, power level, and formula so the MDES output is interpretable.

The synthetic observational stand-in's generating hypothesis is unspecified. If it is drawn from the same 'Power-law mass with independent spin' model as the sim catalog, the KS result is trivially null; if from a different model, trivially significant. For pipeline-verification mode this is acceptable, but the generating distribution should be stated (and ideally distinct from the sim hypothesis) so the verification run exercises both significance paths.
